correctness.rationale: The independently reconstructed multivariate CLT has exchangeable independent Gaussian limits because the fixed coordinate logarithmic increments have equal finite mean/variance and independent coordinates. The dth-order Gaussian gap is positive almost surely, hence the unscaled rank gap diverges in probability; on a suffix of length floor(sqrt n), centered fluctuations are o(n^{3/8}) by Chebyshev and the prefix rank is unchanged with probability tending to one. For each integer nonzero Fourier frequency k, the independent suffix selected product has modulus at most q_k^{d floor(sqrt n)}, with q_k<1 uniformly over the fixed m coordinate laws; this proves joint independence of label and circular phase. The exact competing-subset inequality makes V/(2^{m-d}M)->1 in probability. Separate cases d=m and m=1 are covered. Independently checked 14,650 exact fixed-score subset-product and rank-gap inequalities, which do not establish the probability limit.

value.rationale: The original face-product leading-digit conjecture and its heterogeneous extensions are natural questions in random fragmentation. A joint limit that makes the winner label asymptotically independent of leading digits, while explicitly revealing the deterministic dependence between the two phase variables, is a meaningful new refinement. It handles discrete, nonsmooth, nonidentically distributed coordinate laws under only finite second moments, beyond the earlier smooth globally iid theorem; the exact distributional statement would be reusable in such models.
